touches.text: WHY: Each rung adds one thing to the rung below, so a component's place says how complex it is, and the line between rungs is measured, not judged. Without hard boundaries Claude creates a tangled mess that exceeds its own complexity limit long before completion.

Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.

Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
Device: its own process, in the rack, on the bus (2).
Instance: every device has at least one; a singleton is instance 0.
Tools and machines are peers in the tree; the rung is complexity, not rank.
Names here are the names we keep. Where the code still says otherwise, the code changes.

Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code. That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is a script that calls the long form (eg `cairn superclaude` -> `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` -> `cairn recovery show temp`), which also saves the walk from searching farther, or does work itself (eg install). Shortcuts live beside what they serve (RULE 1). `cairn foo` whose first word is not a device means `cairn cairn foo`: top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict. [Q#98: The verdict's instrument run, and the proofs that exercise it, need bubblewrap, which Windows does not have, so `cairn test --exec` refuses there ("the instance seal is not confirmed ... bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed") and three teeth stay red on Windows: test_the_instrument_is_run (two teeth) and the standing-verdict-proofs-stay-green check. Measured 2026-11-13. Whether Windows gets its own seal is the per-OS seal question in Q#90 (9.4.2.3.3); this one is the narrow choice that stands beside it: until that is settled, do the bwrap teeth skip on Windows (and read as not-run there), or do they stay red until Windows has a seal of its own?]

conflicts.ticket_says: A ref under bin/ yields a non-None domain; the rung 'bin' carries a charter that declares the placement
conflicts.why: Section 5.4.3.3 describes bin/ as 'just its list of shortcuts' — a directory of scripts beside devices and machines, not a component with a charter on the complexity axis. If bin/ is only a collection of shortcuts (not itself a rung), then refs like bin/cmd/proofgate should not have a domain; they're inside a device's or machine's shortcut directory, not at rung-level.
